1. CONFIRMED — rootGlob is a dead clause: the model can never report a root-glob conflict, contradicting both its own prose and pathsOverlap.
spec-writeset-admission.tex:452-457 (Store) and :507-512 (AdmitMission), first disjunct:
  "(open\ i).isDir = (open\ j).isDir \land (open\ i).truncLen > 0 \land (open\ j).truncLen > 0 \land ( (open\ i).rootGlob = ztrue \lor (open\ j).rootGlob = ztrue \lor ... )"
ENTRY (:328-330) defines rootGlob = ztrue iff #pattern = 1 and pattern(1) = wildRestSeg, and in exactly that case truncLen = #pattern - 1 = 0. So rootGlob = ztrue implies truncLen = 0, and the conjunct truncLen > 0 makes the "rootGlob = ztrue \lor ..." disjunct unsatisfiable. The rootGlob field can never fire in any conflict.
The narrative at :470-474 asserts the opposite: "a root glob on either side overlaps unconditionally (``an entry whose FIRST segment globs claims from the root'')".
The code disagrees too. pathsOverlap (conflict.go:266-275) guards emptiness WITH the root escape included:
    if (len(as) == 0 && !aRoot) || (len(bs) == 0 && !bRoot) { return false }
    if aRoot || bRoot { return true }
Concrete divergence: entry A = `**` (ws-file, truncLen 0, rootGlob ztrue), entry B = `docs/**` (ws-file, truncLen 1). Code: overlapSegments("**") returns ([], true), so aRoot → pathsOverlap returns TRUE and admission refuses. Model: disjunct 1 fails on truncLen_i > 0; disjuncts 2/3 require differing isDir; so the invariant permits both entries open simultaneously — NO conflict. A faithful rendering needs ¬((truncLen_i = 0 ∧ rootGlob_i = zfalse) ∨ (truncLen_j = 0 ∧ rootGlob_j = zfalse)) in place of the two truncLen > 0 conjuncts. This also means the 7266-state ProB run never exercised the root-glob path, so WriteSetNonOverlap (:587-597) is weaker than the theorem table claims.

2. CONFIRMED — \implies and \comp used in text mode break the pdflatex build.
\implies is \let-bound to \Rightarrow and \comp is a \DeclareMathSymbol in fuzz.sty (lines 291 and 314) — both math-mode-only. The file uses them inside \field{...} (= \texttt{...}), i.e. horizontal text mode, at four places:
  :343  \item The predicate \field{isEI = ztrue \implies isDir = ztrue} is
  :478  invariant forcing \field{isEI = ztrue \implies isDir = ztrue}, also
  :564  the identical \field{segs} = \field{squash(raw \comp unwrap)} from
  :948  \field{ENTRY.isEI = ztrue \implies isDir = ztrue} & validate.go rule
I ran pdflatex -halt-on-error on a copy: FATAL, no PDF produced —
  ! Missing $ inserted.
  l.343 ...ield{isEI = ztrue \implies isDir = ztrue}
The file's own header says "% Compile: pdflatex spec-writeset-admission.tex". None of the three sibling specs (spec-mission-lifecycle.tex, spec-hook-gates.tex, spec-audit-durability.tex) contain this pattern — it is unique to this file. fuzz is unaffected, which is why the type-check passes.

  LaTeX Warning: Reference `sec:opabandon' on page 7 undefined on input line 537.
Output reads "§??–??".

4. CONFIRMED — Scope misstates what lint.go:193's trailing-slash guard operates on, and contradicts §5.2 of this same document.
:80-84: "its trailing-slash guard (line~193) and its own \field{HasPrefix} comparison BOTH OPERATE ON \field{CanonicalPath}'s joined string"
lint.go:193 is `if strings.HasSuffix(w, "/") && strings.HasPrefix(cf, CanonicalPath(w)+"/")`. The HasSuffix guard tests `w`, the RAW write_set entry; only the HasPrefix half touches CanonicalPath(w). The claim is not merely imprecise but self-defeating: CanonicalPath strips trailing slashes (conflict.go:481, 518-524), so a trailing-slash test against its output would be unconditionally false. The document's own sec:validation-8ady (:769-771) states the guard correctly as strings.HasSuffix(w, "/").

5. CONFIRMED — PathContainedByBuggy/Fixed drop the empty-segment-list refusal the real pathContainedBy has.
:383-392 and :404-414 define containedBy = ztrue iff truncLen <= #segs and ..., introduced at :374-375 as "Today's real pathContainedBy (conflict.go:360--379) and segmentsContain (conflict.go:394--419), specialized to a single trailing **". The real function opens with (conflict.go:363-365):
    if len(fs) == 0 || len(es) == 0 { return false }

The author clearly knew of this rule — it is modelled in the admission half as the truncLen > 0 conjuncts — so its absence here is an oversight, not a declared abstraction (it appears in no Non-goal at :89-126).

:872-877: "That combined run explores 7266 states, 43180 transitions --- the identical state count the isolated run below finds, WITH MORE TRANSITIONS BECAUSE PathContainedByBuggy/Fixed FIRE AS ADDITIONAL ENUMERATED SCHEMAS without contributing any new Store state", and :881-883 gives the isolated Init/AdmitMission/ReleaseMission run as 7266 states, 35915 transitions.

Either the 35915 figure is wrong or the isolated scratch file enumerated an extra operation the prose does not disclose; as written the explanation cannot be true. The same 35915 figure is repeated in the WriteSetNonOverlap theorem row (:594-596) and the tool-run table (:900-901).

(a) :469-470: "the first is ws-dir x ws-dir or ws-file x ws-file". entryPairConflicts's default branch, which this disjunct models, is documented in the code as covering three rows (conflict.go:212-214): "Both directories (ws-dir × ws-dir, ws-dir × ei-dir) or both files (ws-file × ws-file)". ws-dir x ei-dir appears nowhere in the paragraph's walk-through, so :468-485 accounts for only 5 of the 6 rules it sets out to enumerate. (b) :473-474 attributes the quotation "an entry whose FIRST segment globs claims from the root" to conflict.go:303--305. That string is at conflict.go:254-255 (inside pathsOverlap's doc comment); lines 302-305 are overlapSegments's different wording ("has no literal prefix at all ... reported as a root claim").
(c) :827-828 cites conflict.go:339--340 for the file name docs/audited-delegation.md in pathContainedBy's doc comment; it is at conflict.go:338. Lines 339-340 are the following clause.

8. PLAUSIBLE (low severity) — "Three separate probcli runs" contradicts the tool-run table.
:616: "Three separate probcli runs back the claims above." The Tool-run table (:892-914) lists six model rows, two of which are additionally run at two setsizes each; and sec:validation-admission alone describes two runs (committed file as a whole, plus the isolated scratch file). The count is wrong under any reading — "three demonstrations" would be defensible, "three runs" is not.

Quoted: "\field{ReadChunkVerified}'s per-chunk hash check (audit\_seal.go:189--193)"

Prose: "A line is then never inside any one checkout's working tree, so `git worktree remove` cannot reach it structurally, regardless of which checkout is removed or when."
Z: `WorktreeRemoveD1 / Xi AuditLineD1 / where writerExists = ztrue / -- pure frame: removing A checkout has nothing left to take from the per-machine spool.`

Consequence — writerExists = zfalse is unreachable anywhere in Design 1's state space, and the guard writerExists = ztrue is trivially always true. I confirmed this pinning is exactly what produces the reported 9 states / 42 transitions: with writerExists fixed to ztrue there are 8 concrete states (2 pool configs x hookInstalled x rosterKnown) + 1, and 40 + 2 transitions. That version is the one that actually demonstrates the prose claim, and it would change D1's reported counts.

spec-writeset-admission.tex:452-457 (Store) and :507-512 (AdmitMission), first disjunct:
  "( (open\ i).isDir = (open\ j).isDir \land
      (open\ i).truncLen > 0 \land (open\ j).truncLen > 0 \land
      ( (open\ i).rootGlob = ztrue \lor (open\ j).rootGlob = ztrue"
ENTRY at :328-330 sets rootGlob = ztrue iff #pattern = 1 and pattern(1) = wildRestSeg, and in exactly that case truncLen = #pattern - 1 = 0. So rootGlob = ztrue implies truncLen = 0, and the truncLen > 0 conjunct makes the rootGlob disjunct unsatisfiable.
The prose at :470-474 claims the opposite:
  "a root glob on either side overlaps unconditionally (``an entry whose FIRST segment globs claims from the root'', conflict.go:303--305)"

    if (len(as) == 0 && !aRoot) || (len(bs) == 0 && !bRoot) { return false }
